approachQuestion.prompt:
Hub broadcast. A directed graph has V vertices numbered 0 through V-1 and is given as read-only adjacency lists. Return the number of vertices reachable from a start vertex, including start. There are 1 <= V <= 200,000 vertices and at most 400,000 listed directed edges; self-loops and cycles are allowed, duplicate edges are not. The adjacency list for a vertex is directly accessible and each neighbor reference costs constant time to read. All vertices are valid. Choose minimum deterministic worst-case total time, then asymptotic peak auxiliary storage. Storage offers a zeroed boolean array with allocation/initialization cost proportional to its length and a queue with constant-cost enqueue/dequeue and linear peak storage in its live items. Return only a count.

Example 1: Input: adjacency=[[1],[2],[1],[]], start=0. Output: 3.
Example 2: Input: adjacency=[[],[0]], start=0. Output: 1.

options.text: Allocate V false marks. Mark start and enqueue it; repeatedly dequeue a vertex and enqueue each still-unmarked neighbor only after marking it. Count vertices when first marked.
options.feedback: Marking before enqueue makes each reachable vertex enter once despite cycles. Only outgoing lists of reached vertices need to be read.

options.text: Allocate V false marks and use an explicit depth-first stack. Mark vertices when pushing them and expand each popped vertex’s adjacency list once.
options.feedback: This visits exactly the same reachable vertices and outgoing edges, with the same asymptotic worst-case costs as the marked queue method.

options.text: Run a marked reachability traversal separately from every vertex and retain all reachable sets, then answer for start.
options.feedback: It gives the right count but solves many unrequested searches and retains a global reachability table. Only one start was requested.

options.text: Enqueue start, then repeatedly enqueue every outgoing neighbor without any visited marks; count dequeued items until the queue is empty.
options.feedback: For adjacency=[[0]], the self-loop repeatedly re-enqueues start and the process never finishes, although the required count is 1.

feedback.reason: Account separately for global mark initialization and work on the subgraph actually reached.
details: Allocate and initialize V false marks. Mark start, enqueue it, and initialize count=1. Dequeue each pending vertex and examine its adjacency list; for each unmarked neighbor, mark it immediately, increment count, and enqueue it. Return count when the queue is empty. Retain no copied adjacency lists.

Mark a neighbor when enqueuing it, so two incoming edges cannot queue duplicate copies. Only lists reached from start are scanned, but initialization still touches all V marks. A graph with many unreachable edges does not force visiting those edges under this adjacency-list method.

“Allocate V false marks. Mark start and enqueue it; repeatedly dequeue a vertex and enqueue each still-unmarked neighbor only after marking it. Count vertices when first marked.”: Marking before enqueue makes each reachable vertex enter once despite cycles. Only outgoing lists of reached vertices need to be read.

“Allocate V false marks and use an explicit depth-first stack. Mark vertices when pushing them and expand each popped vertex’s adjacency list once.”: This visits exactly the same reachable vertices and outgoing edges, with the same asymptotic worst-case costs as the marked queue method.

“Run a marked reachability traversal separately from every vertex and retain all reachable sets, then answer for start.”: It gives the right count but solves many unrequested searches and retains a global reachability table. Only one start was requested.

“Enqueue start, then repeatedly enqueue every outgoing neighbor without any visited marks; count dequeued items until the queue is empty.”: For adjacency=[[0]], the self-loop repeatedly re-enqueues start and the process never finishes, although the required count is 1.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze mark-before-enqueue. Let R be the reachable vertex count and E_R the number of edges listed out of those R vertices. Choose tight worst-case total time and auxiliary space, including initialization of all V marks. Do not count edges listed only out of unreachable vertices. The boolean marks are ordinary allocated storage, not a pre-initialized input; no hashing or recursion is used.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard bound for the complete execution. Count peak simultaneously live auxiliary storage; exclude supplied input and required output.
Word arithmetic, indexing, and copying one fixed-size element take constant time. No hashing or recursion is used.

options.text: O(V + E_R) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(R + E_R) time, O(R) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space, where E is the entire graph edge count

feedback.reason: Initialize V marks, then scan only reachable adjacency entries.
details: Zeroing the mark array costs O(V). Each reachable vertex is queued once and its outgoing edges examined once, adding O(R+E_R); R<=V gives O(V+E_R). Unreachable outgoing lists are never scanned. The V marks dominate auxiliary space, with at most R queued vertices. Input adjacency lists are excluded and are not copied.
“O(R + E_R) time, O(R) auxiliary space”: This omits zeroing and storing all V marks, even when the reachable component is tiny.
“O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space, where E is the entire graph edge count”: This is a valid loose upper bound, but unreachable outgoing edges add no traversal work, so E_R is tighter.
“O(V²) time, O(V²) auxiliary space”: The method neither constructs a reachability matrix nor examines every possible vertex pair.
